text: Have you ever picked up an ordinary stone on a beach and noticed a faint, ribbed pattern shaped like a tiny shield?
nxt: You might brush it off as a trick of erosion.

title: Three Lobes
text: The name simply means three lobes.
nxt: A central axial lobe ran down the back, flanked on each side by a pleural lobe that sheltered the legs and gills.

title: Three Lobes
text: Their bodies were also divided lengthwise into a head shield, a flexible segmented thorax, and a tail.
nxt: This modular design was an evolutionary masterpiece.

text: Beneath that armor, a trilobite looked more like a living machine.
nxt: It carried a pair of long antennae at the front, and under each segment a pair of jointed legs.

title: Eyes of Stone
text: Perhaps the most astonishing marvel sat right on their heads. Our eyes are made of soft living tissue.
nxt: Trilobite eyes were built from solid calcite, a crystal form of calcium carbonate.

title: Eyes of Stone
text: Imagine looking at the world through hundreds, or in some species more than ten thousand, tiny rock lenses.
nxt: Because they were mineral, those lenses did not rot after death, so scientists can still study their optics today.

title: The Rolled-Up Fortress
text: The ancient ocean was full of danger, so many trilobites learned a trick you can still see in garden pill bugs,
nxt: which are unrelated crustaceans. They rolled up into a tight ball.

title: The Ordovician Peak
text: Surprisingly, the Ordovician was one of the peaks of trilobite variety. Warm seas, rich in food, spread across the continents,
nxt: and trilobites split into a huge number of forms, each fitted to a different way of life.

title: The Ordovician Peak
text: They were swimmers, burrowers, and crawlers, hunters and scavengers. At that moment, it seemed nothing could stop them.

title: The First Freeze
text: No golden age lasts forever. Around four hundred and forty-five million years ago came the Late Ordovician mass extinction.
nxt: Massive ice sheets spread across the southern continents, locking away water and causing sea levels to plummet worldwide.

title: The First Freeze
text: The shallow shelves where trilobites thrived shrank, and the water cooled. Many families vanished.
nxt: Yet the survivors pulled through, proving that their design could outlast a planetary freeze.

title: An Arms Race
text: When the climate settled, the oceans grew more dangerous than before.
nxt: Giant sea scorpions prowled the bottom, and cephalopods with sharp beaks hunted nearby. Later, the first armored, jawed fish arrived.

title: The Devonian Crisis
text: Reef systems collapsed, and trilobite families disappeared one after another.
nxt: Vast dead zones spread across the seafloor, choking the muddy habitats that trilobites called home.

title: One Branch Left
text: The flamboyant giants, the spiny monsters, and the bizarre spade-nosed scavengers were gone.
nxt: The proetids were mostly small, modest creatures with oval bodies, generalists clinging to life in the remaining shallow waters. They had weathered the storm.

title: Holding On
text: For well over a hundred million years, through the Carboniferous and the Permian, the proetids held on.
nxt: On land, vast swampy forests formed the coal beds that power our factories today.

title: A Fragile Remnant
text: Think about what that meant. Each earlier crisis had taken away more than species.
nxt: It had taken away whole ways of living: the swimmers, the giants, the spiny defenders, the burrowing watchers.

title: A Fragile Remnant

nxt: A group that once filled the world ocean with thousands of forms had been reduced to a quiet remnant. It had survived, but it was fragile.

title: The Great Dying
text: The final act began about two hundred and fifty-two million years ago, at the end of the Permian.

title: The Great Dying
text: It was not a single fiery instant. The evidence points to a long, grinding crisis that unfolded over many thousands of years.

title: Fire from Siberia
text: What triggered it? Massive volcanic eruptions in what is now Siberia, known as the Siberian Traps.
nxt: Over a very long time, they flooded the landscape with basalt, a few million cubic kilometers of it.

title: Fire from Siberia

title: Fire from Siberia
text: Scientists think the magma also burned through coal and carbonate rocks, releasing enormous amounts of carbon dioxide and other gases.
nxt: The climate warmed sharply, and the oceans grew far hotter than anything life there had known.

title: An Acid Ocean
text: As carbon dioxide dissolved into the sea, the ocean became more acidic.
nxt: For animals with shells made of calcium carbonate, that was a serious problem.

text: Trilobites were bottom dwellers. When the mud beneath them turned toxic, they had nowhere left to go.

title: Why No Escape
text: Why couldn't they adapt one more time? No one knows for sure.
nxt: But evolution needs time and variety, and the Devonian crisis had pruned the trilobite family tree down to one narrow branch.

title: The Last Trilobite
text: When the last one stopped moving, a dynasty that had watched complex animal life rise quietly slipped into eternity.

title: A Success Story
text: We often think of extinction as failure. But is that fair? Look at the numbers.

title: A Success Story
text: Trilobites thrived for about two hundred and seventy million years. They adapted to nearly every corner of the sea, and they developed crystal vision.
nxt: Our own species has existed for about three hundred thousand years.

title: A Success Story
text: By that measure, trilobites were not a failure. They were one of the greatest success stories in Earth's history.

title: Living Cousins
text: Trilobites left no direct descendants, but their relatives are all around us.
nxt: A horseshoe crab scuttling along a muddy shore at low tide is not a trilobite descendant.

title: A Stone on the Shore
text: The next time you walk along a quiet shore and pick up a smooth stone, look at it with curiosity.
nxt: Run your fingers across its cool, ridged surface and remember the silent travelers who may once have called that rock home.
